tutorial.title: Creating Your Own Python Modules
tutorial.descriptionContent: Create focused Python modules and import them without unwanted behavior.
tutorial.shortDescriptionContent: Python learners who know functions and standard-library imports

lessons.title: Two Copies, One Problem
lessons.interactiveContent:
A weather app and a trip planner each keep the same conversion function. A correction needs two edits, so the copies can drift apart.

You'll replace both copies with one shared Python file that each program can reuse.

lessons.title: One Shared Python File
lessons.interactiveContent:
temperature.py becomes a module when another file imports it. A focused module can keep related constants and functions together.

Add the descriptive constant name FREEZING_POINT_C.

Make sure to pick FREEZING_POINT_C.

lessons.title: Name the Module
lessons.interactiveContent:
The clear filename temperature.py describes one responsibility. Its members use equally descriptive names.

Add DEFAULT_CITY as a related default for the temperature app.

Make sure to pick DEFAULT_CITY.

lessons.title: Import the Module
lessons.interactiveContent:
Sibling files can work together. Python uses import temperature to load definitions from temperature.py.

Complete the guided import in script.py.

Make sure to pick import temperature.

lessons.title: Use the Namespace
lessons.interactiveContent:
The import creates a temperature namespace. Namespaced access connects the function call to its source module.

Add temperature before the function name.

Make sure to pick temperature.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The import creates a temperature namespace. Namespaced access connects the function call to its source module.

Import the shared module and store the Fahrenheit conversion of 20 in result.

Make sure to pick import, followed by temperature, temperature, and finally celsius_to_fahrenheit.

lessons.title: Share a Constant
lessons.interactiveContent:
The module also defines FREEZING_POINT_C. Access the constant through the same namespace.

Make sure to pick temperature.FREEZING_POINT_C.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Import the module and check whether its FREEZING_POINT_C constant equals 0.

Make sure to pick import, followed by temperature, FREEZING_POINT_C, and finally ==.

lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the code access through the temperature namespace?

The module's conversion function.

lessons.title: Reuse the Shared Code
lessons.interactiveContent:
The trip planner needs Kelvin temperatures. Complete the call to the new function in the shared module.

Make sure to pick temperature.celsius_to_kelvin.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The trip planner needs Kelvin temperatures. Complete the call to the new function in the shared module.

Make sure to pick import, followed by temperature, and finally celsius_to_kelvin.

lessons.title: Keep the Module Focused
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which file keeps one clear responsibility?

temperature.py contains conversion functions and temperature constantstemperature.py contains conversions, trip messages, and account settings

temperature.py contains conversion functions and temperature constants.

lessons.title: Choose the Clear Module
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which module name clearly describes functions that convert temperatures?

temperature.pytools.pystuff.py

Make sure to pick temperature.py.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which module name clearly describes functions that convert temperatures?

temperature.pytools.pyweather_app.py

Make sure to pick temperature.py.

lessons.title: Keep the Module Name
lessons.interactiveContent: A namespace keeps each imported name connected to its module. This makes the source clear when several modules use similar names.

lessons.title: Import One Function
lessons.interactiveContent:
When a file needs one member, from ... import ... brings that selected name directly into script.py.

Select celsius_to_fahrenheit from temperature.py.

Make sure to pick celsius_to_fahrenheit.
lessons.hardModeContent:
When a file needs one member, from ... import ... brings that selected name directly into script.py.

Import the Fahrenheit conversion function directly from the shared module.

Make sure to pick from, followed by import, and finally celsius_to_fahrenheit.

lessons.title: Call It Directly
lessons.interactiveContent:
A directly imported function doesn't need the module name before it. Complete the call with the function name.

Make sure to pick celsius_to_fahrenheit.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A directly imported function needs no module prefix. Complete the import and call to convert 20 Celsius to Fahrenheit.

Make sure to pick from, followed by temperature, import, celsius_to_fahrenheit, and finally celsius_to_fahrenheit.

lessons.title: Import a Constant
lessons.interactiveContent:
Selected imports work for constants too. Add the constant name after import.

Make sure to pick FREEZING_POINT_C.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Selected imports work for constants too. Import the freezing-point constant directly from the shared module.

Make sure to pick from, followed by import, and finally FREEZING_POINT_C.

lessons.title: Compare the Styles
lessons.interactiveContent:
A namespace call keeps the source module visible, while a directly imported function uses a shorter call.

Add temperature to complete the namespaced call and compare both styles.

Make sure to pick temperature.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A namespace call keeps the source module visible, while a directly imported function uses a shorter call.

Complete both imports so the namespaced call and direct call work.

Make sure to pick import, followed by temperature, and finally from.

Which name can script.py call directly after this import?

Make sure to pick celsius_to_kelvin().
lessons.hardModeContent:

Make sure to pick celsius_to_kelvin().

lessons.interactiveContent:
Import the conversion function and freezing-point constant in one statement.

Make sure to pick celsius_to_fahrenheit,, followed by FREEZING_POINT_C.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Import the conversion function first and the freezing-point constant second in one statement.

Make sure to pick from, followed by import, celsius_to_fahrenheit, and finally FREEZING_POINT_C.

lessons.title: Switch Import Styles
lessons.interactiveContent:
The weather app only needs one conversion. Complete the direct import and its call.

Make sure to pick from temperature import celsius_to_kelvin, followed by celsius_to_kelvin.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The weather app only needs one conversion. Complete the direct import and its call.

Make sure to pick from, followed by temperature, import, celsius_to_kelvin, and finally celsius_to_kelvin.

lessons.hardModeContent:

lessons.interactiveContent:
A program needs only celsius_to_kelvin() from a focused temperature module. Which statement matches that plan?

from temperature import celsius_to_kelvin.
lessons.hardModeContent:

lessons.title: A Surprise During Import
lessons.interactiveContent:
script.py imports the module, but the module's demo message appears before the app result.

Import temperature to see that it triggers code that the app didn't request.

Make sure to pick import, followed by temperature.
lessons.hardModeContent:
script.py imports the module, but the module's demo message appears before the app result.

Import temperature and choose the Celsius input that makes the app result 77.0.

Make sure to pick import, followed by temperature, celsius_to_fahrenheit, and finally 25.

lessons.title: Top-Level Code Runs
lessons.interactiveContent:
The function show_demo() is run when the file is imported because there is a top-level call defined below it, so the import runs it.

Complete the top-level show_demo() call that causes the demo output.

Make sure to pick show_demo().
lessons.hardModeContent:
The function show_demo() is run when the file is imported because there is a top-level call defined below it, so the import runs it.

Define show_demo() to display "Demo", then complete its top-level call.

Make sure to pick def, followed by "Demo", and finally show_demo().

lessons.title: Separate the Demo
lessons.interactiveContent:
Reusable definitions can stay at the top level. The demo can call the conversion function; we just need to be aware of this behavior.

Add celsius_to_fahrenheit(20) inside show_demo().

Make sure to pick celsius_to_fahrenheit(20).
lessons.hardModeContent:
Reusable definitions can stay at the top level. The demo can call the conversion function; we just need to be aware of this behavior.

Add celsius_to_fahrenheit(20) inside show_demo().

Make sure to pick celsius_to_fahrenheit, followed by show_demo, and finally 20.

lessons.title: Meet __name__
lessons.interactiveContent:
To prevent unwanted function calls, we can use Python's special __name__ variable, which stores the file's current role.

Type __name__ to inspect this special variable's name that changes based on whether the file is started or imported.

Make sure to type __name__.

lessons.title: Direct Run Means __main__
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we run temperature.py, it becomes the entry point. Python deliberately sets its __name__ to "__main__".

Check if __name__ is set to "__main__", meaning that this file is Python's entry point.

Make sure to pick "__main__".

lessons.title: Direct Run Means __main__ - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use this check to guard specific function calls. When the file runs directly, the condition is True, so show_demo() runs.

Check whether this file is the entry point by checking __name__'s value.

Make sure to pick ==, followed by "__main__".
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can use this check to guard specific function calls. When the file runs directly, the condition is True, so show_demo() runs.

Check whether this file is the entry point by checking __name__'s value.

Make sure to pick __name__, followed by if, ==, and finally "__main__".

lessons.title: An Import Keeps the Module Name
lessons.interactiveContent:
When script.py imports temperature.py, Python sets __name__ inside it to "temperature", its normal module name.

That differs from "__main__", so the guard is false, and the demo stays quiet. Complete the import to see it in action.

Make sure to pick import temperature.

lessons.title: Build the Main Guard
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the condition that is true only when temperature.py runs directly.

Make sure to pick "__main__".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the condition that is true only when temperature.py runs directly.

Make sure to pick __name__, followed by if, and finally "__main__".

lessons.title: Guard the Demo Call
lessons.interactiveContent:
show_demo() is already defined. Place its call inside the main guard.

Make sure to pick if __name__, followed by == "__main__":, and finally show_demo().
lessons.hardModeContent:
Put __name__ on the left of an equality check for direct execution, then call show_demo() inside the guard.

Make sure to pick __name__, followed by ==, "__main__", and finally show_demo().

Nothing will be printedIt prints Demo: 68.0It prints temperature

lessons.title: Run the Module Directly
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when temperature.py itself runs directly?

The guard is true, so the demo runsThe guard is false, so the demo is skipped

The guard is true, so the demo runs.
lessons.hardModeContent:
What happens when temperature.py itself runs directly?

The guard is true, so the demo runsThe guard compares the filename and skips the demo

The guard is true, so the demo runs.

lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete both files. In temperature.py, protect the demo with "__main__".

In script.py, add both import styles so the function and constant are available.

Make sure to pick import followed by temperature and then temperature, temperature.
lessons.hardModeContent:

Make sure to pick import, followed by temperature, from, celsius_to_fahrenheit, and finally FREEZING_POINT_C.
